findings.headline: Review this createSignal(fn) call: a function first argument now creates a writable derived signal.
findings.why: Solid 1.9.13 stored this call's first argument as the signal's initial value, so a function was returned literally by the getter, but Solid 2.0.0-rc.21's "new function forms" section reads a function first argument as a derived computation (createSignal(fn) returns a writable derived signal; createStore(fn, seed) returns a derived store), so the signal now runs the function and tracks its reactive reads.
findings.guidance: Decide whether a derived signal was intended. If a function value was intended, wrap it in another function (createSignal(() => theFunction)) or store it elsewhere (a plain let, a ref, or an object property that this signal holds) so the getter returns the function itself. If a derived signal was intended, keep the call as is and confirm every reader is prepared to re-run on tracked changes. Stop without proposing a change when the intended value shape is unclear, when the callback reads reactive state with its own timing, or when consumers observe the function identity rather than its result.
